content.narrative_hook: An old hand offers to share his sluice line — but only if you work the upstream end, where the colour is thinner and the labour heavier.

beats.text: He leans on his windlass handle, watching you pan. You've been at it an hour for nothing.
"I got colour here," he says, tipping his pan. A few flakes catch the light."
"You take upstream, I take downstream. We split even." His eyes don't blink.
Everyone knows the upstream end is a duffer — but it's better than nothing.

neutral.text: Whatever you decide, the old hand files your answer away for later.

options.label: Accept the partnership
options.description: Take the upstream end — thin colour is still colour.

options.label: Decline and keep your own ground
options.description: You didn't come here to work someone else's claim for scraps.

options.label: Propose a different split
options.description: Offer to take upstream only if the split favours you downstream.
